meta: Dramas like Because This Is My First Life: six quiet adult romances about rent, work and saying the thing.
standfirst: A contract marriage between a woman who needs a room and a man who needs a mortgage paid, and sixteen episodes in which the obstacle is money and self-knowledge rather than a rival. The register is the draw: dry, unhurried, and about three couples negotiating what they actually want out loud. These six live in that register, and we say which ones keep the negotiation and which reach for a plot.

picks.why: The same exhaustion, with the romance stripped back further. Lee Min Ki again, three siblings commuting from the edge of the city, and a show about a life that is fine and unbearable at once. Both treat the real enemy as the commute, the rent and the sense of being slightly behind. Difference: it is the slowest thing on this site by a distance, the first four episodes are close to nothing, and it offers no contract, no plot and no comfort.

Four adults who talk like adults, and the talking is the show. A sprinter, a translator and two second leads at least as good as the first pair, all solving their problems by saying what they mean. Same absence of a villain, same interest in what a healthy relationship actually sounds like. Difference: no marriage contract and no housing plot, so it has less structure holding it together and drifts more.

Adult romance shot like a European film. A pharmacist and a librarian, both of them already tied to other things, moving at the speed of two people who know exactly what leaving costs. Same taste for silence, family pressure and conversation as the entire action. Difference: it is a melodrama about breaking up rather than a comedy about moving in, and there is no wit in it at all.

Two people who already know each other, filmed being interviewed about it. Ex-sweethearts dragged in front of a documentary camera, with the interview device doing the same job the contract does here: forcing two guarded people to state a position. Difference: it is about four episodes of story stretched to sixteen, and it is far more interested in beauty than in logistics.

Same director, ten years younger. Nam Sung Woo again, on college athletes falling in love with no jealousy engine and no misunderstanding held for four episodes. Same conviction that a couple being direct is more watchable than a couple being kept apart. Difference: it is broad, goofy and about twenty year olds, so the money and marriage anxieties that drive this one do not exist.

Same director, the fluffiest thing he has made. Park Joon Hwa on an actress hiding as a secretary in a law firm, built almost entirely from Lee Dong Wook being stiff at Yoo In Na. Same pleasure of two people negotiating a fake arrangement into a real one. Difference: there is no engine under it, and the per-episode ratings fall through the second half because sixteen hours is too long for the joke.

against.title: Business Proposal
against.why: The contract-relationship recommendation by default, and it is a good time. It is also a live-action cartoon at twice the speed, where every beat is farce. First Life's whole method is deadpan restraint, and the two do not scratch remotely the same itch.

against.title: Marriage, Not Dating
against.why: The go-to fake-marriage title, and that is where the resemblance stops. It runs on jealous ex-girlfriends, meddling mothers and misunderstandings held for episodes at a time, all of which First Life pointedly refuses.

against.title: What's Wrong with Secretary Kim
against.why: Suggested for the workplace-plus-cohabitation shape. It is a power fantasy about a narcissist being softened, played at high pitch, and the plot underneath it is optional. First Life is about two equals with no money and no leverage.
